Christina on why Vanta pays its top people 10x what it did five years ago

"Should I adjust the pitch and be like 'Inevitably the baseline here is Vanta's 50 billion. 

The real question you should be considering is if you join, can you take us on a journey to 250 billion?’

Should I start saying that? Probably not. But the answer is not definitely not. 

Because that is the pitch that people who work at Vanta are getting from other companies. The market now is saying that so much, you do seem unambitious.

Total comp, it's probably like a factor of 10. I think it actually should be higher. My general comp philosophy is you never pay the top people enough.

Patrick: What those top people are doing that's so valuable typically.

High agency, get shit done. That sounds so milquetoast and that's worth millions of dollars, but yes, actually it is. 

A high-context person who understands the company and the customers and the domain, making generally reasonable decisions and sometimes bad ones, and then iterating on their bad ones and just moving is so valuable."

Christina Cacioppo on why French software companies have stopped building on American models:

"I was very surprised to learn a lot of the French software companies are using Chinese models predominantly.

I was with our customers in France...and someone said, 'We all switched to Chinese models when Trump closed Fable off to non-Americans. 

We just realized there's a huge business continuity risk. 

We can't trust that if we build a business on one of these American models, it'll always be available, so we stopped doing that.'"

tweets.text:
In 2015, Boualem Sansal won the Grand Prix du roman de l’Académie française for 2084, published the same year as Michel Houellebecq’s Submission.
Sansal’s novel offered, in fact, a far darker and more pessimistic vision of the future. He imagined a religious totalitarian regime that maintains its grip on society through the manipulation of language, censorship, and, perhaps most importantly, les "non-dits," everything people are taught never to say, question, or even think about. Sansal was particularly interested in how a regime could erase historical memory so thoroughly that submission eventually feels natural. An Algerian writer of Kabyle Berber heritage and a fierce critic of the FLN regime, he was imprisoned by the Algerian authorities in 2024 and spent nearly a year behind bars while battling cancer before his release in 2025. I had the great honor of meeting his lawyer.

the fact that one of Bitcoin's most infamous skeptics has now turned into a long-term bull speaks volumes if you ask me.

#Graphene $HGRAF
20 October 2026

An 8.28 km sea bridge. Saltwater. Humidity. Relentless UV.

Graphene-enhanced anticorrosion coatings are now protecting China’s Xiangshan Port bridge. According to the developer, they can double the service life of conventional coatings—potentially cutting maintenance costs and extending the life of critical infrastructure.

Today’s coverage strengthens why I’m bullish on HydroGraph’s opportunity in protective coatings.

The economics are compelling: a relatively small material addition could protect assets worth vastly more than the coating itself. Longer maintenance intervals mean fewer shutdowns, less labour and fewer expensive repairs.

HydroGraph is pursuing this market through its collaboration with Sparc, testing its Fractal Graphene in protective coating formulations.

The Chinese project has no disclosed HydroGraph involvement. For me, its significance is evidence that graphene coatings are reaching substantial infrastructure applications.

Bridges, ports, ships, pipelines and offshore structures all face the same costly enemy: corrosion.

HydroGraph still needs to turn technical progress into commercial orders. But this deployment reinforces my conviction that protective coatings could become one of its most valuable markets.

https://t.co/vEMNrn8tKQ

Investors are watching to see what you do right after they write the check.

Pop some champagne, sure or in my case sparking apple juice. But then get back to building.
